question: A fund started with 127 dollars donated. They added 19 dollars Monday. They added 61 dollars Tuesday. They multiplied by 4 through grant matching. They added 45 dollars from a raffle. They added 8 more dollars from tips. They removed 666 for charity work. The organization employed 5 people. How much money remained in the fund?

On Monday morning Dalia counted 229 pairs of shoes in her stockroom, which is bigger than the one her colleague Emre looks after. 6 pairs were water-damaged and were thrown out before the shop opened. In the afternoon a delivery van brought 27 more pairs into the stockroom. That evening head office asked for 8 branches to each hold as many pairs as Dalia's stockroom. The company then tripled that whole order to get ready for the sales. How many pairs of shoes does the company's order come to?

In the morning the foreman at a bolt factory starts up 7 machines, each of which makes 209 bolts in an hour, along with an old hand press that adds 70 bolts in an hour. In the afternoon the whole setup runs for exactly 5 hours, and the factory repeats this same schedule on each of 6 days to fill an order. In the evening of the last day, the foreman adds 77 bolts from the storeroom to the order. Each machine cost 1200 dollars when it was bought. How many bolts are in the order?

A creamery filled 110 churns, with 4 buckets of milk going into every churn and 9 litres in every bucket. All of that milk was then run off into containers that each hold 4 litres. The creamery sold 868 of those containers at the Saturday market. A dozen cats sat waiting by the dairy door. The creamery's records are kept in litres rather than in gallons. How many containers are left?

A community garden had 125 tomatoes ready to pick at the start of the week. A volunteer picked 68 more tomatoes the next day. The garden coordinator mentioned a dozen new watering cans had also arrived, though that had nothing to do with the tomato count. Another volunteer picked 38 more tomatoes, and a third added 59 more to the harvest bin. A fourth picked 34 more, all within a stretch the coordinator described as '120 minutes, or two hours' of picking. At the end of the week, 196 tomatoes were donated to a local food pantry. How many tomatoes were left after the donation?

In the morning, a factory had 112 units. By afternoon, production increased 7 times. By evening, 188 units were removed. They removed 536 units. Finally, they added 43 units. How many units do they have?

A warehouse received shipments throughout the day. Morning inventory: 223 items. Then 3 items arrived. Production multiplied by 5 for the afternoon shift. An additional 73 items came in. The total was doubled for evening count. Then 25 more arrived. Plus 55 final items for next-day processing. How many items are in the warehouse at day's end?

A farm stand began the morning with 109 pumpkins, while a dozen scarecrows stood watch nearby, unrelated to the count. By midmorning, 59 pumpkins were sold. By midday, 7 more pumpkins were added from a late pick. In the afternoon, 51 more pumpkins were added. A festival order required the stand to prepare 4 times that afternoon total. By evening, 7 more pumpkins were added from a final harvest. How many pumpkins did the stand have by evening?

In the morning Cam sold 126 cups of lemonade at his stand and then 10 more. His stand is 4 metres long. In the afternoon he counted that every cup sold for 2 dollars, that is two hundred cents. He sold the same number of cups every day for 7 days. In the evening of the last day he spent 1673 dollars on a new bicycle. How many dollars does Cam have left?

A manufacturer produced components. Starting batch: 114 items. Multiplied by 9 for production run. Added 6 specialty parts. Multiplied by 7 for assembly. Multiplied by 6 for distribution. Morning, afternoon, evening production. A dozen baseline items noted. How many distributed?

A restaurant served 232 meals on opening day. They removed 133 from the counter for catering. They multiplied the remaining meals by 3 for weekend prep. They multiplied by 2 for holiday events. They added 68 meals from new menu items. They added 71 pre-ordered meals to the kitchen. They had planned to serve 500 customers this month. How many total meals were prepared?

For each screening of the new film, the Lyric cinema sells 52 tickets online and 29 tickets at the door. The film, which runs for 112 minutes, is shown 6 times every day. In addition, 37 free passes are used at the cinema each day. This schedule continues for 5 days. How many people attend the film over the 5 days?

A warehouse had 118 boxes. They doubled to 236. They multiplied by 8 to 1,888. They added 3, reaching 1,891. They multiplied by 5 to 9,455. They added 44, reaching 9,499 boxes. His facility has 10,000 capacity (not exceeded). How many boxes total?

In the morning, a bakery had 109 loaves of bread. By midday, a rush order multiplied the loaves sevenfold, even though a different bakery across town reported baking 2,000 loaves that same morning. In the afternoon, 603 loaves were sold to a catering company. By evening, a matching order tripled the remaining loaves. Overnight, a final wholesale deal multiplied the loaves eightfold. How many loaves were in the bakery by the next morning?

Two camp counselors, Petra and Julius, tracked kayak counts, and Julius's fleet always trailed hers. Petra's fleet started with 176 kayaks. A donation added 63 more kayaks, unrelated to the 100 life jackets stored separately in the shed. A rental company delivered 12 more kayaks. A late gift added 3 more kayaks. A regional donation added 23 more kayaks. A final delivery added 51 more kayaks. How many kayaks did Petra have in her fleet?

A factory tracked output. Starting production: 224 items. He added 15 rush orders. He subtracted 165 for recall. He multiplied by 9 for next week's demand. He added 72 bonus items. Working through morning, afternoon, and evening. How many items projected for next week?

In the morning, Diego had $218 saved in his savings account. By midday he had earned $49 more from a weekend job. That afternoon, a bank promotion doubled the money in his account. In the evening, a birthday check for $69 arrived and was added to his balance. Right before the bank closed for the night, a final loyalty bonus turned every dollar in his account into 6 dollars. How much money was in Diego's savings account after the loyalty bonus was applied?

The wire depot counted 203 rolls in the yard when it opened in the morning, and a supplier dropped off 10 more before eight. A dozen workers were on the early shift. Every roll on the rack is drawn out into 9 straight lengths. During the afternoon each length was chopped into 4 shorter pieces on the bench saw. In the evening every piece was bent into 4 hooks for the garden centre order. How many hooks did the depot make?

A used bookstore had 126 novels on its clearance shelf, and the owner added 31 more from a donated box. A book club then bought in bulk for branch libraries, leaving the shelf with 8 times as many novels. 41 books were later returned as damaged and pulled from stock. A regular customer mentioned the store was about a dozen steps from the coffee shop, unrelated to the books. The delivery van spent 90 minutes on the road, roughly an hour and a half, on a special drop-off. 71 more books then arrived from an estate sale, and 65 more came in from a closing school library. How many novels did the store end up with?

A business scaled rapidly. Starting capacity: 99 units. He subtracted 97 for maintenance. He added 68 new equipment. He multiplied by 8 for efficiency gains. He multiplied by 9 for scale. He multiplied by 8 for redundancy. Converting to labor hours, how many hours of production?

Ollie has 47 nickels in his piggy bank. His sister Pia has twice as many nickels as Ollie. Since a nickel is worth 5 cents, Pia worked out the value of her nickels in cents. She then added 42 cents in pennies to her savings and spent 134 cents on a comic. How many cents does Pia have left?

A construction crew started the morning with 130 bricks stacked at the site. By midmorning, a delivery truck added 69 more bricks. At midday, the crew organized the bricks into 8 identical pallets, each holding that same amount, combining them for a wall project. In the afternoon, a second shipment required 8 times that combined total for a bigger job, and since the crew measures bricks by count but the supplier invoices by weight, the foreman kept a conversion sheet handy. That evening, a final order required 7 times that afternoon total. Overnight, 7 more bricks were added from a returned pallet. How many bricks were on site the next morning?

In the morning, a shoe factory had 222 pairs of sneakers ready to ship. By midday, 131 pairs were sent to a retail chain, and in the afternoon a return shipment brought back 72 pairs due to a sizing error. The shipping manager mentioned a dozen extra shoeboxes had also arrived, though that had nothing to do with the pair count. That evening, a rush order turned every pair into 8 pairs. Right after, 70 more pairs arrived from the factory floor, and before the night shift ended, 78 more pairs were finished. A final bulk order turned every pair into 8 pairs. How many pairs of sneakers were there after the final bulk order?

In the morning 8 boxes of floor tiles, each holding 162 tiles, arrived at a renovation site, and the tiles were shared equally among the 4 tilers working there. In the afternoon the foreman gave Ana, one of the tilers, 40 extra tiles from the van. Ana laid all of her tiles in 4 equal rows across the hallway floor, which took her half an hour. The hallway is 5 metres wide. In the evening she measured the next room and found it would need 7 rows of exactly the same size as those hallway rows. How many tiles does Ana need for the next room?

A business had 13 items. Their partner had 100 items. They added 76. They multiplied by 9. They multiplied by 6. There was a loss of 1071 items. The work took 120 minutes, or 2 hours. They multiplied by 9. How many items?
